desc:
AI research agents for competitor and market notes gather, compare and summarize information from the sources you approve, with a link back to each fact. Ecom Swift LLC builds the agent around your questions, so research that took hours arrives as a short, checkable brief.

## What slow manual research costs you

Checking competitor prices, reading supplier pages and following industry news is useful work, and it is easy to put off. Pages change, tabs pile up, and notes end up scattered across documents. By the time a comparison is finished, part of it is already out of date.

The result is that decisions get made on old or partial information. A price change goes unnoticed, a new competitor appears without comment, or a supplier quietly alters its terms. A research routine that runs on a schedule keeps your picture current without a person doing the legwork each time.

## What is an AI research agent?

A research agent is an automated assistant that visits a set list of sources, extracts the facts you asked for and writes them up. It does not browse the whole internet at random. It works from a research brief: a written question, the sources it may use and the format of the answer.

Each fact in the output carries a source link and a date. That is the core design choice. A summary you cannot check is a risk, while a summary with links lets you verify anything in a few seconds.

## How research agents improve decisions

The main effect is time and consistency. The same question is asked the same way every time, so changes show up clearly. A weekly digest tells you what moved since last week, instead of you hunting for it.

The agent also shows disagreement. When two sources give different figures, a well-built agent flags the conflict instead of choosing one silently. That helps you decide what to verify by hand. Better information leads to better pricing, product and supplier choices, though the quality of the sources you approve always limits the quality of the result.

## What a good research agent includes

- A written research brief for each question, in plain words.
- An approved source list that you control and can extend.
- Respect for each site's rules, including no collection of anything a site forbids.
- A summary that links every fact to its source page.
- A date for each fact, so stale information is obvious.
- A side-by-side comparison table for competitors, products or suppliers.
- A flag when sources disagree or when a fact is missing.
- A review step where a person confirms the important findings.
- Output as a document, a sheet, an email or a chat message.
- Scheduled runs and an alert when a tracked fact changes.

## What we do

We start with the questions you ask most often, such as "what are three competitors charging for this product?" or "what changed in supplier terms?" For each one we write a brief and agree the source list with you.

Then we build the agent, test it on questions where you already know the answer, and compare its output with yours. We adjust the instructions until the facts and the links match. The Basic package builds one brief on demand. Standard adds several briefs, comparison tables and source dating. Premium schedules the research, sends a weekly digest, alerts you to changes and teaches you to add sources yourself.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Choose sources you trust and that allow automated reading.
- Write each question so it has a checkable answer.
- Open the links on important facts before acting.
- Review the source list every so often and remove weak ones.
- Keep a person responsible for final decisions.

**Avoid:**
- Treating the summary as fact without checking the source.
- Asking one vague question that covers many topics.
- Using sources that block automated access.
- Collecting personal data about individuals.
- Expecting the agent to find information that is not on the approved pages.

## Who this is for

This service suits a store owner who tracks competitor pages and wants a regular comparison. It suits a consultant who prepares market notes for clients each week. It also suits a buyer who watches several supplier sites for changes in availability and terms.

## What we need from you

Share your research questions, the sources you want used and an example of the output you would like. Give us access to the document, sheet or chat tool where the results should go as a collaborator, team member or developer user, wherever supported. We never ask for passwords.
